tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Mean value characterization]1. ch2:2.7\group chapter-2 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0033 ↗ gt.thm2.6 ↗ gt.thm2.2 ↗ gt.thm2.3 ↗ gt.thm2.4 A continuous function $u$ is harmonic in $\Omega $ if and only if every ball $B_R(y)\Subset \Omega $ satisfies \begin{equation} \tag {2.30} u(y)=\frac{1}{n\omega _nR^{n-1}}\int _{\partial B_R(y)}u\, ds. \end{equation}
Proof

↗ gt.thm2.6 ↗ gt.thm2.2 ↗ gt.thm2.3 ↗ gt.thm2.4 \sketch Necessity is Theorem 1. Conversely, solve the Dirichlet problem on each ball using Theorem 26. The difference between $u$ and that harmonic solution has the mean value property and zero boundary values, so the maximum-principle argument forces it to vanish.

□
